conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening tool called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. Everything you share stays between you, me, and the clinical team; nothing leaves this room unless safety requires it. We’ll go through ten gentle questions about the past seven days—no right or wrong answers, just whatever feels true for you. Ready to begin?

Over the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

Hi, Sarah. I’m ready.

Um… I guess I’ve still laughed a little—like if my partner does something silly—but it doesn’t come as easily. Mostly I feel kind of flat, so when something’s funny I have to remind myself to chuckle. It’s not impossible, just… harder than before the baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’ve laughed a few times, but it doesn’t come naturally right now. I sort of have to force it, and the moment fades fast.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get little sparks of excitement—like when my mom said she’d come help or when I planned a short walk—but they’re smaller and burn out quickly. Mostly I’m just getting through the day rather than really looking forward to anything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. Like, if the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle her right away, I immediately think it’s because I’m not doing something right or I’m not “in tune” enough with her. Rationally I know babies just cry, but in the moment my brain jumps to “This is my fault.”
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll be feeding her and suddenly feel this wave of worry—like, what if she’s not gaining enough weight or what if I miss some sign that she’s sick—and there’s no real reason for it. I can usually talk myself down pretty quickly, but it pops up out of nowhere a couple of times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky… just a tight, fluttery feeling in my chest when the “what-ifs” hit. It’s uncomfortable, but I can breathe through it and it passes in a few minutes.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, a few days this week I’ve felt like the pile of tiny tasks—laundry, bottles, diapers, texts I haven’t answered—just stacks up faster than I can clear it. I end up thinking, “How am I the only adult here keeping this show running?” I still manage, but it feels heavier than it should.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, I wouldn’t say I’m that unhappy. I do sometimes lie there after a night-feed, mind racing about tomorrow’s to-do list, so it takes me a while to drift back off—but once I’m asleep I stay asleep.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I’d say maybe three or four days this week I’ve had that dragging, gray feeling. It’s not constant—there are moments of okay-ness—but the sadness sneaks in, especially in the evenings when the house gets quiet.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times—once when the baby wouldn’t nap and once when my partner found me folding laundry at midnight. It wasn’t all-day sobbing, just sudden tears when the stress bubbled over, and I felt better after a few minutes.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed and tired, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Patient: Postpartum mother, self-report on EPDS-10 items  

<sym>Symptoms endorsed</sym>  
- Diminished pleasure/enjoyment (Q1, Q2)  
- Unwarranted self-blame / guilt (Q3)  
- Recurrent anxious intrusive thoughts, 2–3× daily (Q4)  
- Brief chest tightness / “fluttery” panic sensations, no full attacks (Q5)  
- Feeling overwhelmed by routine infant-care tasks (Q6)  
- Intermittent low mood / “gray” days, 3–4 in past week (Q8)  
- Episodic tearfulness under stress (Q9)  

<sym>Symptom profile</sym>  
Mild-to-moderate severity: symptoms present but manageable, no impairment in basic functioning; no anhedonia pervasive enough to meet major criteria; no suicidal ideation (Q10 denied).  

<med>Risk indicators</med>  
- Perinatal mood and anxiety concern (PMAD) screen positive for mixed depressive-anxiety features.  
- Sleep-onset difficulty linked to racing thoughts rather than frank insomnia secondary to mood (Q7).  
- Absence of self-harm ideation → no immediate safety concern.  

<lab>Observation</lab>  
Patient demonstrates situational coping skills (self-talk, breathing) and social support; nevertheless, persistent worry, guilt, and episodic sadness/weepiness warrant closer monitoring and possible referral for structured assessment and supportive intervention.
